title: Replace the engine air filter
summary: Swap the paper element that filters intake air. One of the easiest jobs on any car.
interval: Typically every 20,000 miles or two years. Sooner if you drive on dusty or rural roads.
safety: Engine off and cool. Nothing here needs the engine running.
Do not drop anything into an open intake. Anything that goes down there gets eaten.

tools.name: Screwdriver or socket set
tools.note: Many airboxes are clip-only and need no tools at all.

steps.title: Find the airbox
steps.detail: A large black plastic box, usually near a corner of the engine bay, with a thick trunking hose running out of it towards the engine.

steps.title: Release the lid
steps.detail: Undo the spring clips and any screws. Leave the intake trunking attached if you can — just flex the lid up.

steps.title: Note how the old filter sits
steps.detail: Look for an airflow arrow or a rubber seal that faces a particular way. Photograph it before you lift it out.

steps.title: Remove the old element and wipe out the box
steps.detail: Leaves and grit collect in the bottom. Wipe it out with a damp cloth — do not wash the box out with the trunking connected.
steps.warning: Do not let debris fall into the outlet side of the box. That side leads straight to the engine.

steps.title: Fit the new element
steps.detail: Seal seated fully all the way round. If the lid does not close without force, the filter is in wrong.

steps.title: Close and secure the lid
steps.detail: All clips latched and all screws in. An unsealed airbox draws in unfiltered air and can upset the airflow sensor.
